claim_ceiling: The publication reports study-specific isotope enrichment in a four-arm controlled Petri-dish experiment. It includes a no-receiver arm, an isotope-only non-inoculated receiver arm and a natural-abundance arm, but no donorless arm and not the full isotope-control factorial for the no-receiver condition. 15N-amino-acid enrichment in receiver plants can reflect root uptake from fungal exudates/necromass; it is not identified as direct hyphal transport. D2O plant enrichment is confounded by an abiotic signal in isotope controls. No universal CEN law or field-scale rate is established.
control_gaps: No donorless treatment was included, so donor-plant dependence cannot be measured directly.
The +E/+I/-R no-receiver arm did not have the full isotope-control set (examples identified by the authors: -E/-I/-R and -E/+I/-R).
The -E/+I/+R isotope control and -E/-I/+R natural-abundance control do not fill the missing no-receiver factorial cells.
13C and 15N moved independently; 13C cannot be used as a proxy to estimate amino-acid-derived 15N movement.
F. temperatum receiver-soil 15N enrichment means direct hyphal transfer cannot be separated from fungal exudate / necromass and receiver-root uptake.
Plant D2O enrichment also occurred in isotope controls; fungal treatment differences relative to that isotope control were not significant.
